subject: Post-demo: technical sync — JSON schema safety & retry tasks
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@brightfoundry.io>, Asha Roy <asha@brightfoundry.io>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 21 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo: technical sync — JSON schema safety & retry tasks

Hi Samir / Asha — thanks again for the demo time this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so engineering can start scoping: 

Recap (call highlights)
- Primary goal: surface-safe structured summaries from models for downstream systems (order records, approvals). BrightFoundry needs strict schema guarantees + clear retry behavior on schema failures.
- Non-functional constraints: EU data residency for PII, sustained ~250 req/s during business hours, 95th pct latency target ~300ms for inference.
- Auth: BrightFoundry prefers signed JWTs for service-to-service calls; procurement wants an IP allowlist option.

Suggested engineering next steps (for review)
1) Schema proposal: Redwood to share a proposed canonical JSON schema for the 3 response types we demonstrated (order_summary, risk_flags, trace_metadata). Karthik will attach an initial draft.
2) Constrained decoding + validation: agree on a runtime pattern — model configured with enforcement tokens/stopping heuristics, then validate on Redwood side and apply deterministic repairs or reject.
3) Retry and backoff: define retry policy for transient model responses vs hard schema failures. Recommend exponential backoff with jitter for network/transient model errors; do not auto-retry on deterministic validation failures without a remediation attempt.
4) Routing: default to hosted (low-latency) with fallback to dedicated for heavy batch backfills. We should propose a routing policy for production.
5) Embeddings/reranker: confirm if BrightFoundry will run embeddings in-house (preferred) or via Redwood. If in-house, we'll provide the embedding interface and the JSON schema for the reranker contract.

Actions / owners
- Karthik: attach schema draft + example SDK snippet for bootstrapping auth (due EOD Mon).
- Priyom: write short note on validation vs repair strategies and link to example instrumentation (due Tue).
- Vanessa (me): schedule technical deep-dive next week and handle procurement intro.

Proposed times for deep-dive: Tue 11/23 10:00–11:00 PT or Wed 11/24 09:00–10:00 PT. Please pick a slot or send alternatives.

Attachments: BF-implementation-milestones.pdf (high-level timeline).

Thanks — looking forward to the follow-up.

—
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@brightfoundry.io>

Date: Sun, 21 Nov 2027 13:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: technical sync — JSON schema safety & retry tasks

Vanessa — thanks, this is helpful. Quick clarifications from our side so the tech deep-dive can be focused: 

Constraints from BrightFoundry engineering: 
- Data residency: all PII/evidence must remain in EU (we can accept inference in US for non-PII but prefer EU hosted option).
- Throughput: baseline 250 req/s with spikes to 600 for peak reporting windows.
- Auth: signed JWTs issued by our internal auth server; we prefer mutual TLS for the dedicated path.
- Failure policy: procurement will not accept silent data mutation; any automated "repair" must be auditable and reversible.

Requests before deep-dive:
- Can you send an example schema and a sample validation failure payload? We want to see how Redwood surfaces the error and what fields are logged.
- Latency SLOs for hosted vs dedicated variants (p50/p95).

Also copying procurement (procurement@brightfoundry.io) so they can flag anything contract-related early.

Samir
VP Product Engineering
BrightFoundry
